newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran blasts Israeli-Palestinian deal on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Iran blasts Israeli-Palestinian deal on Hebron.

text.p: Iranian state radio on Wednesday slammed an accord between Palestinian and Israeli leaders to extend Arab rule to the West Bank town of Hebron, saying it would fail to halt the Palestinians' fight against Israel.

"This latest accord can be seen as an...effort by the designers of the compromise (peace process) to delay the crisis in the talks," Tehran radio said. "Its only aim is to prevent a rise in the struggles of the Palestinian people."

"But there are major obstacles and solid reasons which discredit the optimism of those who designed this compromise," the radio said. "There are no prospects that these issues will be resolved peacefully."
It was commenting on the decision recahed by Palestinian President Yasser Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu at the Erez crossing between Israel and Gaza early on Wednesday.

The radio said there were no guarantees Israel would carry out its commitments while difficult issues remained unresolved, including the status of Jerusalem and the problems of Palestinian refugees and of Jewish settlements on the West Bank.
Iran, which says Israel has no right to exist, has condemned the peace process as a sell-out of Palestinian and Arab rights.
Tehran has denied Israeli and U.S. charges that it has sponsored terrorism, saying it only gives political and moral support to Palestinian groups opposed to the peace accords.
